title: Tooling landscape
summary: Because the GenAI conventions ride on OpenTelemetry, one instrumented app can feed Application Insights, Langfuse, LangSmith, Phoenix or a local dashboard. Pick the backend by ecosystem, the features you need around traces and where your data may live.
useIf: You must choose, combine or replace a tracing and evaluation backend for LLM applications.
avoidIf: You pick a tool for its demo and discover later that its transport, data residency or pricing does not fit.

explain.md: OTLP is the common door. Backends differ in what they accept and what they add on top of traces: dashboards, evaluation, prompt management and data controls. Check the transport first, then the features, then where data lives [[r17]] [[r18]] [[r19]] [[r14]]. Because the format is shared, you instrument once and choose the backend by configuration, and an OpenTelemetry Collector can fan the same spans out to several backends during a migration [[r18]].

Expect attribute mapping, because the GenAI conventions are still evolving: Langfuse maps received OTel traces to its own data model and supports popular GenAI attributes. To filter or aggregate by user or session there, those attributes must be on every span, not only the root, and baggage with a span processor is the documented way, with the warning not to put sensitive values in baggage [[r17]].

How traces arrive

rows: Langfuse
OTLP at `/api/public/otel` (traces at `/api/public/otel/v1/traces`), HTTP/JSON or HTTP/protobuf, Basic auth, regional endpoints [[r17]]
gRPC is not supported, so a default gRPC exporter fails
LangSmith
`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=https://api.smith.langchain.com/otel` plus an `x-api-key` header, optional `Langsmith-Project` [[r18]]
Give the base URL only: the exporter appends `/v1/traces`, and including it returns 404. Regional and self-hosted hosts differ
Arize Phoenix
Accepts OTLP, built on OpenTelemetry with OpenInference instrumentation, with tracing, evaluation, prompt tools and experiments [[r19]]
OpenInference attributes are a second vocabulary beside `gen_ai.*`
Application Insights and Foundry
Microsoft OpenTelemetry Distro or Foundry server-side tracing, KQL, Agents (Preview) view, Grafana dashboards [[r12]] [[r14]]
Agents view and some dashboards are preview; sampling defaults apply

pitfalls.symptom: Langfuse shows nothing from a default Agent Framework Python app
pitfalls.cause: The framework's default OTLP exporter uses gRPC and Langfuse accepts only OTLP over HTTP
pitfalls.fix: Set the protocol to http and use the `/api/public/otel` endpoint with the required headers [[r17]] [[r10]]

pitfalls.cause: The endpoint included `/v1/traces` on a base-URL setting, so the exporter appended it again
pitfalls.fix: Set the base `https://api.smith.langchain.com/otel` and let the exporter add the path [[r18]]

scenarios.title: An Azure-only company with agents in Foundry
scenarios.situation: A company runs everything in Azure. Agents are hosted in Foundry plus a few services on Container Apps. Security wants data to stay in the tenant. The team has KQL experience.
unknowns: Are workflow agents in use (preview paths)?
Is an eval workflow needed on top of traces?
scenarios.question: Which backend do you choose?

options.name: Foundry tracing with Application Insights, plus OTel export from the container services
options.why: It keeps data in the tenant, covers hosted agents with no code and gives KQL and Grafana.
options.tradeoff: Preview parts remain, and eval workflows are less polished than eval-first tools.

options.name: A hosted SaaS eval platform for all traces
options.why: It moves trace data out of the tenant, which security ruled out.
options.tradeoff: Right when residency rules allow and evals are the main need.

options.name: Self-hosted open-source tool in the tenant
options.why: Keeps data in your tenant and adds eval features.

flips.if: Eval and prompt workflows become the top need
flips.then: Add an open-source tool in the tenant and fan out through a collector.
Keep OTLP instrumentation and revisit the backend.

scenarios.takeaway: Let ecosystem and data control decide before features.

scenarios.title: A research team iterating on prompts across clouds
scenarios.situation: A small team runs agents across two clouds and iterates on prompts weekly. They want datasets, experiments and trace views, and have no platform engineers.
constraints: Eval and prompt iteration is the need
scenarios.question: How do you set up tooling?

options.name: Vendor-neutral OTLP instrumentation sending to a managed eval-centric backend
options.why: Little to operate, quick datasets and experiments and the backend can change later.
options.tradeoff: Data handling and pricing depend on the vendor.

options.name: Build dashboards on a collector and Grafana
options.why: It needs platform work the team does not have and gives no eval workflow.
options.tradeoff: Right for teams that already run observability platforms.

options.name: Self-host an open-source backend
options.tradeoff: Operations load for a team without platform engineers.

scenarios.takeaway: Small teams buy what they cannot afford to operate.

quiz.q: A Python agent using the default OTLP exporter sends nothing to Langfuse. What is the most likely cause?
options: The default exporter uses gRPC and Langfuse accepts only OTLP over HTTP
Langfuse requires prompts to be stored first
The agent has too many tools
quiz.explain: Langfuse supports OTLP over HTTP with JSON or protobuf and does not support gRPC. It does accept OpenTelemetry, and prompts and tool counts are unrelated.

quiz.q: Match each backend to a documented onboarding detail.

pairs.r: OTLP over HTTP at `/api/public/otel`, no gRPC
Built on OpenTelemetry with OpenInference instrumentation
Local viewer with OTLP on 4317 and UI on 18888

quiz.explain: These are the documented onboarding details checked on 2026-10-13. Mixing them up leads to the 404 and gRPC failures listed in the pitfalls.

quiz.q: Security requires that no trace data leave your Azure tenant, but the team wants evaluation workflows. Which choice fits best?
options: A hosted SaaS tool for all traces
Application Insights plus a self-hosted open-source eval tool inside the tenant
Send traces to a public endpoint with content capture on
quiz.explain: Data control rules out hosted SaaS, and the eval need rules out nothing. A tenant-hosted combination meets both. Disabling tracing loses the evidence and a public endpoint with content is the opposite of the requirement.

flashcards.front: Which transport does Langfuse accept for OTLP?
flashcards.back: HTTP with JSON or protobuf at `/api/public/otel`. gRPC is not supported.

flashcards.front: How should you set the LangSmith OTLP endpoint?
flashcards.back: `https://api.smith.langchain.com/otel` as a base URL with an `x-api-key` header. Do not add `/v1/traces` because the exporter appends it.

flashcards.front: What is Arize Phoenix built on?
flashcards.back: OpenTelemetry, with OpenInference instrumentation. It offers tracing, evaluation, prompt tools and experiments.

flashcards.front: How do you stay vendor neutral?
flashcards.back: Instrument with OpenTelemetry and OTLP, keep content policy outside the vendor choice and use a collector to fan out when migrating.
